After dividend distribution tax. FAQ Section What is SBI Large Cap Fund (Formerly known as SBI Bluechip Fund)? It is an open-ended equity mutual fund that predominantly invests in large-cap companies (top 100 by market capitalization). How can I invest in SBI Large Cap Fund (Formerly known as SBI Bluechip Fund)? You can invest in the fund either by visiting an AMC or branch office for an offline transaction, or through online modes such as the AMC’s website or the InvesTap Nxt app. Investments can be made as a lump sum or through a Systematic Investment Plan (SIP) , depending on your financial objectives and preferred investment horizon. Who should consider investing in SBI Large Cap Fund (Formerly known as SBI Bluechip Fund)? This fund is suited for investors looking for equity exposure with a relatively moderate risk profile. Although it is an equity fund, its focus on large-cap stocks makes it comparatively more stable than mid- and small-cap funds. Investors seeking steady exposure to well-established companies may consider this scheme. Is SBI Large Cap Fund (Formerly known as SBI Bluechip Fund) suitable for long-term investing? Yes, it is suitable for long-term capital appreciation through equity investing. What is the ideal investment horizon for SBI Large Cap Fund (Formerly known as SBI Bluechip Fund)? As an equity-oriented mutual fund, it may be considered with an investment horizon of at least 5 years to potentially realize its benefits. Is SBI Large Cap Fund (Formerly known as SBI Bluechip Fund) suitable for first-time investors? Yes, it makes a good entry point for novice investors to invest in equities. As a large cap fund, it is less volatile than mid/small caps. Why does SBI Large Cap Fund (Formerly known as SBI Bluechip Fund) predominantly invest in large-cap companies? As per SEBI classification, large-cap funds are required to invest at least 80% of their assets in the top 100 companies by market capitalisation. These companies are typically well-established, financially strong, and hold dominant positions in their industries, supported by robust operations and experienced management. By investing predominantly in large-cap companies, the fund aims to provide investors with exposure to stable, market-leading businesses with strong financial fundamentals. Such companies are generally better equipped to withstand economic cycles, which allows the fund to benefit from the relative stability and resilience of large-cap stocks. What characteristics define the companies held by SBI Large Cap Fund (Formerly known as SBI Bluechip Fund)? The fund invests in companies that are part of the top 100 by market capitalisation within the Nifty 500 universe. These companies are typically characterised by strong fundamentals, established business models, robust brand value, industry leadership, and a consistent track record of earnings growth. How does SBI Large Cap Fund (Formerly known as SBI Bluechip Fund) select stocks for its portfolio? The scheme will follow a combination of top down and bottom-up approach to stock-picking and choose companies across sectors. The scheme will predominantly invest in diversified portfolio of large cap stocks. Large Cap Stocks are – 1st -100th company in terms of full market capitalization. This will be in line with limits/classification defined by AMFI/SEBI from time to time. The scheme will predominantly be actively managed to achieve its investment objective. What investment style does SBI Large Cap Fund (Formerly known as SBI Bluechip Fund) follow? The scheme follows a blend of growth and value style of investing. Can SBI Large Cap Fund (Formerly known as SBI Bluechip Fund) invest outside the large-cap universe? Yes, the scheme may invest Up to 20% in other assets (mid/small cap, debt, etc.), while the large portion of the portfolio minimum 80% is in large cap stocks. How does sector diversification benefit SBI Large Cap Fund (Formerly known as SBI Bluechip Fund)? • Reduces concentration risk • Helps manage volatility • Enhances risk-adjusted returns What are the key risks associated with SBI Large Cap Fund (Formerly known as SBI Bluechip Fund)? Key risks associated with large cap includes: • Sensitivity to macroeconomic trends • Market risk (equity volatility) • Sector risk What is the investment objective of SBI Large Cap Fund (Formerly known as SBI Bluechip Fund)? The investment objective of the Scheme is to provide investors with opportunities for long-term growth in capital through an active management of investments in a diversified basket of large cap equity stocks (as specified by SEBI/AMFI from time to time). There is no assurance that the investment objective of the Scheme will be achieved. What are the top holdings of SBI Large Cap Fund (Formerly known as SBI Bluechip Fund)? How are capital gains from SBI Large Cap Fund (Formerly known as SBI Bluechip Fund) taxed? Capital gains tax on this fund depends on the holding period of the investment. Gains from units held for less than one year are treated as short-term capital gains and taxed at 20%. For investments held longer than one year, gains are considered long-term and are taxed at 12.5% on amounts exceeding ₹1.5 lakh in a financial year.
